title: Where the US-Canada Border Isn't Straight at All #shorts
summary: In the east the US-Canada boundary follows the St. Croix and St. Lawrence rivers and crosses four Great Lakes; from the Atlantic to the Pacific more than half of it runs through water.
tags: why is the us canada border straight
sources: Boundary length 8,891 km (5,525 miles) across North America; over 8,000 monuments and reference points; a 6 metre (20 foot) wide clear vista along the land boundary, 3 m (10 ft) on either side of the line (International Boundary Commission, The Boundary): https://internationalboundarycommission.org/en/about/the-boundary.php

Land boundary 5,061 km identified by a series of straight lines which intersect at boundary monuments; 5,528 boundary monuments; 2,172 km of the land boundary runs through forest where the vista must be cleared on a regular basis; Atlantic to Pacific 6,416 km = 2,878 km land + 3,538 km water (3,538 / 6,416 = 55%); Pacific to Arctic (Alaska) 2,475 km (International Boundary Commission, Did you know?): https://internationalboundarycommission.org/en/the-boundary-and-you/interesting-facts.php

Treaty history: 1783 line from the northwesternmost point of Lake of the Woods due west to the Mississippi; 1818 Convention Article II, Lake of the Woods along the 49th parallel to the Stony Mountains (Rockies); 1846 Oregon Treaty westward along the 49th parallel to the Strait of Georgia, then through Juan de Fuca Strait to the Pacific; 1908 treaty for fuller demarcation; 1925 treaty changed the 49th parallel line from a slightly curved line between monuments to a series of straight lines (International Boundary Commission, History): https://internationalboundarycommission.org/en/about/history.php

Map data: Natural Earth (public domain) https://www.naturalearthdata.com and US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain) https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/carto-boundary-file.html

scenes.narration: In the east, the border barely tries to be straight. It follows the {St. Croix|Saint Croix} and {St. Lawrence|Saint Lawrence} rivers, and cuts through four of the Great Lakes.
From the Atlantic to the Pacific, more than half of the line runs through water.

data.title: Mostly *water*
data.source: Intl. Boundary Commission: 3,538 of 6,416 km in water

scenes.narration: Only out west does it follow one straight line: the {49th|forty-ninth} parallel.
